audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions that Graves's basic attacks cannot pass through units, even though the entry is built around a 550-range mage trying to survive an auto-attacker.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Mel's own minion wave is a hard wall against his primary damage source. For a champion with no dash whose entire defence is spacing, standing behind her wave is the single highest-value habit in the matchup, and it was absent while the text instead told her she simply cannot trade.
audit.corrected: His bullets stop on units — keep your own wave between you and his shotgun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (P: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units')

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places say Smoke Screen blinds Mel's autos: mid 'the second he blinds you with W smoke your autos go dark', whys[3] 'W smoke blinds your autos', wants.foe[2] 'Drop his W smoke screen to blind your autos'.
audit.why: Smoke Screen reduces sight range — it is a nearsight, not a blind. Her attacks still land on what she can see; what she loses is the ability to see him, which matters far more for a ground-targeted 950-range Radiant Volley than for her autos. Framing it as a blind sends the player to the wrong counterplay (attacking anyway) instead of the right one (keeping vision or backing out of the cloud).
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts your sight range, so you lose the target rather than the attack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (W: 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range')

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places call his burst 'the True Grit shotgun double-tap' (spikes[1].text, early, whys[2], wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: True Grit is the armour and magic-resist buff on Quickdraw, not an attack. Riot's text: 'If Graves dashes towards an enemy champion, gain two stacks of True Grit instead.' The real fact worth knowing is the opposite of what the name is being used for — when he dashes AT Mel he arrives with double resistances, so her burst into an engaging Graves lands into his tankiest moment.
audit.corrected: True Grit is Quickdraw's resistance buff, doubled when he dashes toward a champion.

audit.whatIsWrong: End of the Line's terrain detonation is never mentioned, though _missing-interactions flags it for exactly this matchup.
audit.why: The shell detonates after one second OR on colliding with terrain. Against a champion with no dash, Graves aims it into the wall along her retreat path so the explosion arrives where she is running to rather than where she is. That is what Flash is actually for in this lane, and the entry spent its Flash advice on his engage instead.
audit.corrected: He detonates End of the Line off a wall to cut a dashless retreat — hold Flash for that, not the damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns tracks Quickdraw as the window without noting that attacking shortens it.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 but 'hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown', so every free auto he lands on the wave or on Mel buys his escape back early — the window closes faster than a static number suggests. Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1, End of the Line 13s, Collateral Damage 100s. And his real lane cooldown is not a spell at all: the shotgun holds limited ammo and must reload, which is the recurring punish window nothing else in his kit covers.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw 16s but shortened by his autos; Smoke Screen 26s; and the reload is the window worth waiting for.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading and report[3].t both say a spent Rebuttal is gone 'for twenty seconds'.

audit.why: 40.63% over 32 games is the best-sampled matchup in this slice, and the level chart (Mel level 1, skill at 2, Graves 3 through 4-5, skill at 6, Graves first item, Mel two-plus) tracks the entry's own reasoning and the kit. Left alone.

edits.before: Level 1 is yours: at 550 range you poke with Q's barrage and chip free damage before Graves can do anything with one ability. The real prize is your Level 2-3 window — when he steps into the 525-or-so range his shotgun needs to last-hit, fire Solar Snare and root him, then dump Q on top. But respect the turn: the moment he has his E dash (usually level 3), he can roll through your bolts and onto you, and his True Grit shotgun double-tap plus an auto will chunk your fragile health bar harder than your poke chunks his. Hold W for his primary fire and his smoke.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: at 550 range you poke with Q's barrage and chip free damage before Graves can do anything with one ability. His shotgun holds limited ammo and must reload, so that animation is the punish window nothing else in his kit covers. edits.before: This is where Graves takes over. As his shotgun and lethality scale, his E lets him close past your range on demand, and the second he blinds you with W smoke your autos go dark and your Overwhelm stacking stalls. You cannot trade autos with him — his burst out-damages your poke and you have no dash to reset distance. Play around your one root: if he dashes in, Solar Snare him point-blank and W his return fire, then disengage. At Level 6 things even out slightly because Golden Eclipse detonates your built-up stacks from any range, so even a Graves who kites out eats damage on the exit — bank stacks before you ever commit.
edits.after: This is where Graves takes over. As his shotgun and lethality scale, his E lets him close past your range on demand, and Smoke Screen cuts your sight range — you lose the target, not the attack, and cannot aim Radiant Volley at what you cannot see. You cannot trade autos: his burst beats your poke and you have no dash to reset. But his bullets cannot pass through units, so keep your own wave between you and the shotgun. Play around your one root: if he dashes in, Solar Snare him point-blank and W his return fire, then disengage. At Level 6 things even out because Golden Eclipse detonates your stacks from any range, so even a Graves who kites out eats damage on the exit.

edits.before: The late game swings back to you if you survived lane. Once your first AP item is online, your Q chains, Overwhelm accumulates off every poke, and Golden Eclipse executes him from a screen away before his Eclipse/Collector burst and bruiser-ADC tankiness let him reset the duel. Never let him E onto you in a sidelane — fight from range with your team, root anyone who dives, and use R to finish him as he tries to roll out. He wins the brawl; you win the kite if you keep the distance.

notes: Best-sampled matchup in the slice (32 games) and it had no flagged defects, but the two facts that decide it were both absent. First, Graves's bullets cannot pass through units — for a dashless 550-range mage her own minion wave is a hard wall against his entire damage pattern, and the entry instead told her she simply cannot trade. Second, End of the Line detonates on terrain, which is how he cuts the retreat of a champion with no dash; _missing-interactions flags exactly this and the entry spent its Flash advice elsewhere. Also corrected: Smoke Screen was called a blind in three places (it reduces sight range — she loses the target, not the attack, which matters much more for aiming a ground-targeted Radiant Volley), and 'True Grit' was used as the name of his shotgun burst in four places when it is Quickdraw's resistance buff, doubled when he dashes toward a champion — meaning Mel's burst into an engaging Graves lands at his tankiest. Left alone as unverified: the '525 auto range' figure for Graves, since no attack-range stats exist anywhere on disk. Full-layer verdict fields remain uncorrectable through the applier (shared boilerplate, exactly-once rule).
